title: PowerPoint on desktop: Copilot Agent Mode creates executive summary slides
summary: Hold for corrections to the administration guidance. Microsoft documents gradual rollout for Copilot features and allows alternative permissions for licence assignment; the briefing reports rollout mechanics as unstated and a broader permission as required. Its restriction on who can view licence assignments also overlooks read-only administrators.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated rollout mechanics for this Copilot feature.
claims.quote: Copilot features are introduced using a safe deployment model, gradually rolling out to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organization.
claims.fix: Replace 'Microsoft has not stated the rollout mechanics or default for this feature' with 'Microsoft says Copilot features gradually roll out to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organisation. A rollout schedule and default specific to executive summary slides are not stated.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/release-notes.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses reaches user licence assignment.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Users > Active users > Licenses and Apps is the route for checking a user's assignments.
claims.quote: Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section
claims.fix: Give the full route already used in the control row: 'Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses'.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: License Administrator or User Administrator is an appropriate role for assigning user licences.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: A License Administrator or User Administrator is needed to view licence assignments.
claims.quote: Global Reader: View administrator features and settings in admin centers that the Global Administrator can view. The Global Reader can't edit any settings.
claims.fix: Replace 'A License Administrator or User Administrator is needed to view and change assignments' with 'You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licences', as stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/assign-licenses-to-users. Do not claim those roles are required for viewing.

claims.claim: The Graph PowerShell licence-assignment route requires the User.ReadWrite.All permission scope.
claims.quote: Assigning and removing licenses for a user requires the User.ReadWrite.All permission scope or one of the other permissions listed in the 'Assign license' Microsoft Graph API reference page.
claims.fix: Replace the permission clause with 'the Graph PowerShell route requires User.ReadWrite.All or one of the other permissions listed in the Assign license Microsoft Graph API reference'. The reference at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/user-assignlicense identifies LicenseAssignment.ReadWrite.All as least privileged; cite it if naming that alternative.
